title: Clinical and virological characterisation of Oropouche, dengue, and chikungunya during simultaneous co-circulation in the State of Espírito Santo, Brazil: a retrospective observational study

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Clinical and virological characterisation of Oropouche, dengue, and chikungunya during simultaneous co-circulation in the State of Espírito Santo, Brazil: a retrospective observational study》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0055】Understanding how viral load relates to clinical expression in co-endemic settings may provide additional insights into the clinical characterization of arboviral infections and guiding diagnostic strategies. Moreover, integrating clinical and virological data may help identify distinguishing patterns that are not apparent when considering these dimensions separately. Therefore, this study aimed to: (a) compare the clinical and epidemiological characteristics of DENV, CHIKV, and OROV infections in a co-endemic setting; (b) characterize the internal structure of symptom co-occurrence as a multidimensional phenotype; and (c) explore the integration of cross-sectional Ct value patterns with clinical expression. These objectives are sequential: clinical comparison establishes the baseline differences, phenotyping reveals how symptoms organise within each infection, and virological analysis assesses whether molecular patterns are associated with differences in clinical expression. This framework is intended to advance understanding rather than establish validated clinical rules.

【Introduction · p0030】The 2024–2025 expansion of Oropouche virus (OROV) into southeastern Brazil marks one of the largest outbreaks of this Amazonian pathogen documented to date.1 In Espírito Santo state, OROV co-circulated with dengue (DENV) and chikungunya (CHIKV) virus,2 creating considerable diagnostic complexity: all three viruses present with overlapping acute febrile syndromes that are difficult to distinguish clinically without laboratory confirmation.3,4 While DENV and CHIKV are well-established in Latin America,5 OROV has recently expanded beyond its historically endemic range, intensifying both the frequency of outbreaks and the challenges of clinical and epidemiological management in co-endemic settings.4,5

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Clinical and virological characterisation of Oropouche, dengue, and chikungunya during simultaneous co-circulation in the State of Espírito Santo, Brazil: a retrospective observational study》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methods · abstract-2-1】We conducted a retrospective observational study using linked surveillance and laboratory databases from Espírito Santo State, Brazil (2024-2025). We aimed to compare DENV, CHIKV, and OROV infections and to explore their virological correlates. Cycle threshold (Ct) values, used as a relative semi-quantitative proxy for viral RNA levels, were analysed within each virus to characterise temporal dynamics and clinical expression. Multinomial logistic regression identified clinical features associated with arboviral infection; associations between Ct values and clinical domain scores were assessed using multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, and time since symptom onset.

【Added value of this study · p0020】Building on previous comparative studies, our study provides three complementary advances. First, we extend the comparative framework to include CHIKV, the primary clinical mimic of OROV-associated arthralgia, allowing estimation of adjusted associations between musculoskeletal symptoms and arboviral infection. Second, beyond comparing isolated symptom frequencies, we characterized the internal structure of symptom co-occurrence, showing distinct patterns of symptom co-occurrence across infections, providing descriptive information on multidimensional clinical presentation. Finally, we provide, to our knowledge, a detailed characterization of cross-sectional Ct value patterns in a large urban OROV cohort and demonstrate that associations between standardized Ct values and clinical phenotypes differ substantially across arboviruses. Crucially, we identified consistent associations between Ct values and systemic and musculoskeletal clinical phenotypes in OROV that were not observed in the other two infections.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Clinical and virological characterisation of Oropouche, dengue, and chikungunya during simultaneous co-circulation in the State of Espírito Santo, Brazil: a retrospective observational study》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · p0150】Beyond differences in symptom frequencies, symptom co-occurrence revealed distinct patterns across arboviral infections (Supplementary Figure S1). CHIKV showed the most cohesive co-occurrence pattern, characterised by tightly clustered musculoskeletal manifestations. DENV exhibited a more structured pattern centred on gastrointestinal and pain-related symptoms, whereas OROV exhibited a comparatively diffuse network with fewer dominant symptoms clusters. These findings suggest that the three arboviruses differ not only in individual symptom prevalence but also in the overall pattern of symptom co-occurrence. When these features were assessed jointly in multinomial logistic regression models, several clinical features remained independently associated with arboviral infection (Fig. 3). In multinomial logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and time since symptom onset, arthritis was positively associated with CHIKV versus OROV (OR 5·22 [95% CI 4·08–6·68]), as was rash (2·39 [1·83–3·12]). Conversely, nausea (2·98 [2·52–3·53]), vomiting (2·54 [2·01–3·21]), and retro-orbital pain (8·00 [6·69–9·56]) were positively associated with DENV versus OROV. Intense arthralgia was inversely associated with CHIKV versus OROV (0·39 [0·34–0·45]) and DENV versus OROV (0·07 [0·06–0·08]). Direct comparison between CHIKV and DENV reinforced these distinctions, with CHIKV remaining associated with joint-related manifestations and DENV with gastrointestinal features.

【Results · p0155】Sex-specific analyses revealed that heterogeneous associations between sex and clinical manifestations varied across arboviruses (Supplementary Table S5). In DENV, female sex was positively associated with headache (OR 1·46, 95% CI 1·22–1·74), nausea (1·62, 1·43–1·84), vomiting (1·22, 1·04–1·42), and petechiae (1·52, 1·16–2·01), whereas fever was inversely associated with female sex (0·69, 0·56–0·84). In CHIKV, female sex was positively associated with intense arthralgia (1·53, 1·30–1·79), nausea (1·49, 1·26–1·76), petechiae (1·46, 1·09–1·95), retro-orbital pain (1·34, 1·14–1·58), and arthritis (1·23, 1·03–1·47), whereas myalgia was inversely associated with female sex (0·77, 0·64–0·92). No statistically significant associations between female sex and individual symptoms were observed for OROV after adjustment for age.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Clinical and virological characterisation of Oropouche, dengue, and chikungunya during simultaneous co-circulation in the State of Espírito Santo, Brazil: a retrospective observational study》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Fig. 1 · fig1】Fig. 1 Flowchart of dataset construction and participant selection stratified by arbovirus. Records were retrieved from the Laboratory Environment Manager (GAL; RT-PCR-confirmed cases only) and e-SUS Notifica (epidemiological notifications) for the period 2024–2025, linked through deterministic matching based on patient name, date of birth, and mother's name, and filtered according to predefined exclusion criteria. Counts are presented separately for dengue virus (DENV; red), chikungunya virus (CHIKV; green), and Oropouche virus (OROV; blue) at each stage. Key differential patterns include: (i) absence of negative RT-PCR exclusions for OROV, reflecting universal testing during emergence response versus routine sampling for DENV/CHIKV; (ii) higher absolute unmatched records for OROV (n = 7706), consistent with larger notification volume during epidemic peak, though proportional rates were comparable (DENV 25·2%, CHIKV 19·4%, OROV 38·3% of merged records); and (iii) similar proportions of missing Ct values across viruses (0·25–0·62%). The final analytical dataset comprised 10,793 infections: 4058 DENV, 2508 CHIKV, and 4227 OROV.

【Fig. 2 · fig2】Fig. 2 Temporal trends, spatial distribution, and age-specific incidence of arboviral infections, 2024–2025. (A) Weekly distribution of reported cases of chikungunya virus (CHIKV), dengue virus (DENV), and Oropouche virus (OROV) by epidemiological week in 2024–2025. Bars represent the proportion of total notified cases attributed to each virus per week. (B) Municipality-level incidence rates (cases per 100,000 inhabitants) for OROV (blue), DENV (red), and CHIKV (green). Choropleth maps depict the spatial distribution of each virus; municipalities with missing data are shown in grey. (C) Age-specific incidence rates (per 100,000 inhabitants) by sex for each virus, presented as population pyramids. Incidence was calculated using population denominators from the 2022 national census.

【Fig. 3 · fig3】Fig. 3 Forest plot of clinical and demographic features associated with arboviral infections. Panels show adjusted odds ratios (95% CI) derived from multinomial logistic regression models comparing DENV versus OROV, CHIKV versus OROV, and CHIKV versus DENV. All variables included in the model are presented. Values shown are n/N (number of patients with the symptom or characteristic over total cases for each arboviral infection). The vertical dashed line indicates the null value (OR = 1).

【Software and visualisation · p0120】All statistical analyses were performed in R (version 4·4·3). Data processing and visualisation were conducted using established packages within the R ecosystem, including tidyverse (data manipulation), dplyr and tidyr (data wrangling), broom (model outputs), purrr (functional programming), and ggplot2 (visualisation).

【Data sharing statement · p0240】The datasets generated and analysed during this study contain sensitive patient information and are not publicly available in accordance with Brazilian data protection legislation (Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados, LGPD). De-identified analytical data may be made available upon reasonable request to the corresponding author, subject to approval by the relevant ethics committee and execution of a data access agreement. No individual participant data will be shared. All code and statistical scripts supporting the findings of this study are openly available in the Genomics and Viral Ecology Lab (LaGEV) GitHub repository at https://github.com/lagev-ufes/arbovirus-phenotype-architecture.
